chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to go to al-Mufadhal and condole him for Ismail. He said: Convey my greetings of peace to al-Mufadhal and say to him: We have been tried through Ismail and have remained patient, so be patient as we have been patient. We wanted a thing, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wanted a thing, so we submitted to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.الْمُفَضَّل: Al-Mufadhal ibn Umar, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of patience and submission to divine decree in the context of bereavement according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the intimate relationship between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his companion al-Mufadhal ibn Umar, using the death of Ismail (likely the Imam's son or a close relative) to teach the virtue of *sabr* (patience) and *rida* (contentment) with divine decree. It underscores the Shia theological principle that while human plans are subject to change, ultimate submission to Allah's will is the mark of true faith, a concept deeply rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's experience of loss.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/268] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Ali b. al-Hakam from Yunus b. Ya’qub who said:

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام ordered me to go to Mufadhal and condole him for [the death of] Ismail. He [the Imam] said: Convey my greetings of peace to Mufadhal and say to him: We have been tried through Ismail and have remained patient, so be patient the way we have been patient. We wanted something but Allah Mighty and Majestic wanted something else so we have submitted to the command of Allah Mighty and Majestic.
